topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

sections.title: Prerequisites: Neurons as Knowledge Keys
lecture_lines: MLPs function as key-value retrieval systems.
animations: Show MLP architecture block (#FF5733) representing input and retrieval.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Pattern Matching
lecture_lines: Specific neurons act as knowledge keys.
They trigger when encountering specific patterns.
animations: Display a specific neuron key icon (#FFFF33) in the layer.
Animate the input pattern (#FF33FF) overlapping with the neuron key.
Display a connection (#00FFFF) confirming accurate knowledge retrieval.

sections.title: Conceptualizing Memory: The Weights as a Database
lecture_lines: Layer one weights store the key.
Layer two weights store the value.
The system triggers a specific fact.
It outputs the desired retrieved word.
animations: Show grid of weights (#CCCCCC) resembling a database table.
Highlight the first weight layer (#FF5733) storing the key pattern.
Highlight the second weight layer (#33FF57) storing the value facts.
Animate a triggering mechanism (#FFFF33) lighting up the specific fact row.
Display the retrieved word output (#FFFFFF) in a final bubble.

sections.title: Integration: Why MLPs vs. Attention?
lecture_lines: Attention coordinates; MLPs hold the knowledge.
animations: Show attention mechanism (#FF5733) connecting different token nodes.
Show MLP storage (#33FF57) as a dense block of memory.
Animate attention routing signals (#FFFFFF) vs MLP memory activation (#FFFF33).

sections.title: Summary & Visual Conclusion
lecture_lines: MLPs match input patterns to facts.
Activation triggers the stored fact storage.
Facts are retrieved through neuron firing.
animations: Show input pattern icon (#FF33FF) approaching the MLP structure.
Animate the firing of a specific neuron (#FFFF33) upon pattern match.
Display the retrieved fact text (#00FFFF) emerging from the output.
